newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish forestry workers seek four pct wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Swedish forestry workers seek four pct wage hike.

text.p: The Swedish forestry industry workers' union said on Wednesday it was demanding wage increases of four percent in a one-year deal.
The union was also demanding a cut in full-time work hours by 25 hours a year, the union said in a release.
The demand is higher than a November demand from the paper workers' union of a 2.5 percent increase in a one-year contract with 25 hours shorter working time.

The forestry and paper workers' unions belong to the few unions that will negotiate at this point in time when underlying inflation is very low and when October figures showed annualised deflation of 0.1 percent.
The Riksbank, or central bank, is likely to watch coming labour market deals very closely as it several times has expressed concern about wage developments, which potentially could boost inflation.
Swedish wages have also worried the government, which has called upon unions and employers to find a way of controlling wage increases in the future.
Last year, most large unions negotiated relatively high wage increases in deals spanning several years. In 1996, wages are on average expected to rise between six percent and seven percent.
The Riksbank's target is two percent annualized inflation with an allowed deviation of one percent point on either side.
